newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Army major declares himself Sierra Leone leader. [CORRECTED 09:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Army major declares himself Sierra Leone leader. [CORRECTED 09:10 GMT]

text.p: An army major, Johnny Paul Koromah, declared himself head of state in Sierra Leone on national radio on Monday after soldiers seized power in a coup in the West African state. (Corrects to fix spelling of Koromah throughout.)

Koromah proclaimed himself head of state saying the armed forces had to overthrow the government of President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah in the coup on Sunday because of what he called the "cabals and sectional politics" of the regime.
"We the armed forces, as the custodians of state security, had to step in," he said.
Koromah appealed for the release of a Sierra Leone rebel leader held in Nigeria, Corporal Foday Sankoh, and called on him to participate in a new Freetown government.

"We are appealing to the international community and Nigeria in particular to release Corporal Foday Sankoh," said Koromah. "We are inviting Corporal Foday Sankoh to participate in the formation of the new government."
